 ‘Fresh investment will make us the world’s largest refined zinc metal producer’
 The expansion is expected to reduce India’s import bill by nearly $2 billion
 By Suresh P Iyengar 
 Updated - November 17, 2026 at 08:30 PM. × Share
 WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/fresh-investment-will-make-us-the-worlds-largest-refined-zinc-metal-producer/article71711859.ece Copy 
 Amarendu Prakash, CEO, Hindustan Zinc
 Amit Gupta, CFO, Hindustan Zinc
 Hindustan Zinc plans to invest ₹80,000 crore over three to five years to nearly double its production capacity to 2 million tonnes per annum (mtpa). The expansion will cover the entire value chain, from mining to finished metal. In an interaction with businessline , Amarendu Prakash, CEO, and Amit Gupta, CFO of the company, spoke about the investment, funding strategy, cost structure and domestic demand.
 Edited excerpts: 
 What does the ₹80,000 crore expansion mean for HZL?
 Amarendu Prakash: We are already the largest integrated mine-to-metal zinc producer, and this expansion will also strengthen our position in refined metal capacity. The fresh investment will make us the world’s largest refined zinc metal producer, with nearly 15 per cent of the global market share. Zinc capacity will increase to 1.6 mtpa, while lead and silver capacity will rise to 0.4 mtpa and 1,500 tonnes per annum, respectively. Rajasthan will be a major beneficiary. We currently contribute about ₹6,000 crore annually to the State’s exchequer, and this will nearly double as the expansion progresses.
 Does the investment include backward integration?
 The entire investment covers the value chain, from ore mining to finished metal. It includes mining, processing and smelting capacities. We have sufficient reserves and resources to support the proposed 2-million-tonne capacity, with a mine life of more than 25 years at the expanded production level. We will continue exploring our existing resources and remain open to acquiring additional mining assets. However, we can achieve the proposed expansion through our existing assets. We have also completed the core work for establishing the BK Mine (Bamnia Kalan Mine in Rajasthan), for which we already have a lease. It is expected to provide an additional 3.5 million tonnes of ore as part of the new project.
 Will additional regulatory approvals and land acquisition be required?
 We have the necessary mining assets, although regulatory approvals will be required as and when mining activity expands. Most of our mines are underground, and the infrastructure will largely be built on land we already have. Some additional land may be required for auxiliary services, and the process is already underway.
 How will the company fund the investment, and will it affect dividend payout?
 Amit Gupta: We currently have net cash of over ₹12,000 crore and do not anticipate taking on net debt to fund the project. The investment will be funded through internal accruals. There is no change in our dividend policy. The funding plan accounts for our existing dividend commitments. The annual expenditure is expected to be ₹10,000-20,000 crore, depending on the peak construction phase and foreign exchange movements.
 What kind of financial returns expected from the expansion?
 We expect revenue to double and EBITDA to double, while broadly maintaining our existing margins. Based on conservative assumptions about London Metal Exchange prices and production costs, we estimate a payback period of five to six years. The ₹80,000 crore investment also includes the previously announced ₹14,000 crore project to add 2.5 lakh tonnes of capacity. That project is progressing on schedule and is expected to be commissioned in the second quarter of FY29, with returns beginning to accrue in FY30.
 Will the expansion affect Hindustan Zinc’s position as a low-cost producer?
 Our production cost guidance remains below $1,000 per tonne, even after the expansion. While deeper mining may involve additional costs, these will be offset by economies of scale and better absorption of fixed costs. The project will also deploy the latest technologies to improve operational efficiency and metal recovery, particularly silver. We are confident of retaining our position as the lowest-cost producer.
 How much of the additional production can be absorbed by the domestic market?
 Prakash: India’s zinc demand is growing at about 7-8 per cent annually. We currently sell about 50,000 tonnes of zinc domestically and expect domestic sales to increase significantly as demand expands. In silver, India consumes about 7,000 tonnes annually, while our current domestic sales are about 700 tonnes. Capacity is increasing to 1,500 tonnes, and we are confident we can sell the entire output in India. At current prices, the incremental silver sales could contribute over $1 billion in revenue. Overall, the expansion is expected to reduce India’s import bill by nearly $2 billion.
 Will renewable energy capacity also be expanded to meet the requirements of the new facilities?
 Gupta: We have already tied up 400 MW of renewable power, which meets nearly 70 per cent of our current requirement. With the proposed expansion, we are looking to tie up another 400 MW. Our objective is to meet around 70-80 per cent of our power requirement through renewable sources. We will follow the captive power model rather than directly investing in renewable energy projects.
